# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;
  `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), `ReelAV1` and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the
  `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) — `ReelCore+Cursor.swift` holds `ReelCursor`
  (`rc_cursor_open`, `rc_cursor_free`: a cursor file's open, which is its check, spec
  §11 CU-9, CU-15; road map creator-jobs CU1a; and `query`, `rc_cursor_query`'s one
  JSON request, CU2, spec §11 CU-25, and the static `query(_:tracks:project:)`, the
  same call over n tracks with a project (`plan_zooms`, CU-70)) — `ReelCore+Framing.swift`
  holds `SpeakerMatch` and `ReelProject.speakerMatch` (`rc_project_speaker_match`, road map
  creator-jobs VR6b, spec §11 VR-65: the face-to-microphone match Make Vertical's sheet
  confirms) — and `ReelCore+Graphics.swift` the graphics engine's
  wrappers (below), with `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`,
  `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`)
  and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)` (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39) — both pure moves
  out of `ReelCore.swift` (road map creator-jobs CJ0d, T15); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join;
  `answer(_:)` hands the tool callback's answer back through
  `rc_agent_string_create` (CJ0d's T15c), a plain static because the trampoline
  runs on the core's server thread, so `AgentServer.swift` names no `rc_*`.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are `ReelCore+Graphics.swift`'s: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize` (and `rasterize(…, deep: true)`,
  `rc_graphic_rasterize_deep`, spec §11 PR-15: a `GraphicRaster` holding
  `rgba16` and an empty `bgra`, `byteCount` what a budget counts),
  `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift`'s `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `cursorURL(for:)` (the
  cursor file: its bookmark when it resolves, else the stored path, existing or
  not), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-nine op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88), and a null range inside `video.qualifier` into
  `video.qualifier.<range>` (GR-36); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eleven names: its twelve arms but
  `add_adjustment_clip`, sent scoped) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op

lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is

traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its

detail there.

content.content:
`UserDefaults`, so every instance a proof drives shares its bundle's
defaults domain with the owner. The guarded domain is the bundle under
test's: `com.kgalligan.FrameJob` for Release, `com.kgalligan.FrameJob.debug`
for Debug (`make app-debug`, spec §11 V-5). A record per socket path holds
that domain's key names against salted digests (`proof_defaults.snapshot`,
`defaults export` only) and the other Frame Job pids sharing it:
`scratch_socket()` records `proof_app.domain()`, the app `RC_PROOF_APP`
chooses, `launch()` re-records the binary's own and owns its child, and
`MCP()` records a socket it was handed. A socket `scratch_socket()` made and
`MCP()` then finds held by an instance of ANOTHER bundle (a script that
started the app itself on it) is re-homed to that bundle's domain, said on
stderr (`_rehome`); a write before that connect is not seen. The record and
the compare both read the domain with no `CFFIXED_USER_HOME` in `defaults`'
environment (`proof_defaults.read_env`): under one naming a folder that does not exist
`defaults export` answers no key, so a script run under a scratch home not
made yet at the record, or removed before the compare, would otherwise be
told every key of the domain moved (issue batch B84; `defaults_proof.py`
H1, H2). `remove_scratch()` compares, and one
`atexit` handler compares every record still held. A moved key outside
AppKit's `NS*`/`Apple*` families prints `mcp: DEFAULTS MOVED in <domain>:
<names> (other Frame Job pids: <list|none>)` on stderr; when no other Frame Job
shares the domain the script ENDS with status `DEFAULTS_EXIT` and those
lines last, and when one does it only prints. A value is never printed.
`defaults_proof.py` is its proof. A handed socket whose file is there and
whose pid `lsof` cannot name is said on stderr, and a moved key is then only
printed unless `lsof` names the pid at the compare. A handed pid whose
bundle identifier cannot be read is said on stderr too: it is owned, and its
record guards the app's domain. A guard body that raised says so on stderr. A domain that cannot be
read is said on stderr. Not reached: a script killed by a signal or leaving
by `os._exit`."""

import atexit
import http.client
import json
import os
import shutil
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time

_HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
if _HERE not in sys.path:
    sys.path.append(_HERE)
import proof_app  # noqa: E402
import proof_defaults  # noqa: E402

MAX_SOCKET_PATH = 103
LSREGISTER = ("/System/Library/Frameworks/CoreServices.framework/Versions/A/Frameworks/"
              "LaunchServices.framework/Versions/A/Support/lsregister")
    try:
        record = _GUARDED.get(socket_path)
        if record is not None:
            if not record["own"]:
                pid = _holder(socket_path)
                domain = _pid_domain(pid) if pid is not None else None
                if domain is not None and domain != record["domain"]:
                    _rehome(socket_path, pid, domain)
            return
        pid = _holder(socket_path)
        if pid is None and os.path.exists(socket_path):
            time.sleep(0.5)
            pid = _holder(socket_path)
        domain = None
        if pid is not None:
            domain = _pid_domain(pid)
            if domain is None:
                _say(f"mcp: the defaults guard could not read the bundle identifier of pid {pid} "
                     f"holding {socket_path}; it guards {proof_defaults.APP_DOMAIN}, which is "
                     "that instance's domain only if it is the real build")
        elif os.path.exists(socket_path):
            _say(f"mcp: the defaults guard found no pid holding {socket_path}; it guards "
                 f"{proof_defaults.APP_DOMAIN} and cannot tell this instance from another "
                 "Frame Job, so a moved key is only printed unless `lsof` names it at the compare")
        _record(socket_path, domain or proof_defaults.APP_DOMAIN, own=[pid])
    except Exception as error:
        _off(socket_path, error)


def defaults_moved(socket_path):
    """Every moved key NAME of that socket's guarded domain since its record
    was made; [] when the socket is not guarded."""
    record = _GUARDED.get(str(socket_path))
    if record is None:
        return []
    try:
        return proof_defaults.moved(record["before"],
                                    proof_defaults.snapshot(record["domain"]))
    except Exception:
        return []


def _moved_line(domain, names, others):
    return (f"mcp: DEFAULTS MOVED in {domain}: {', '.join(names)} (other Frame Job pids: "
            f"{', '.join(str(pid) for pid in others) or 'none'})")


def _unread(domain, socket_path, when):
    return (f"mcp: the defaults guard could not read {domain} {when} (`defaults export` did "
            f"not answer); it cannot see a moved key for {socket_path}")


def _finish(socket_path, record):
    """Compares `record`'s domain now. An owner-visible moved key is appended
    to `DEFAULTS_MOVED` and printed on stderr, and no `Exception` after the
    compare can drop it."""
    try:
        after = proof_defaults.snapshot(record["domain"])

without a checkout: the parent of the commit that ADDED
`app/Sources/LevelMeterView.swift`, or HEAD while the phase is still
uncommitted, extracted with `git archive` into `work/chrome5/before/` and
compiled with its matching Rust core and bridging header, and the SAME
current `harness/main.swift` under `HARNESS_REFERENCE_BUILD`. This preserves
the historical source/FFI contract while using one paint instrument. The answer is
worth the 35 s it costs: at 1440 in both appearances, and at 1080 and 1600,
the TIMELINE BAR differs in exactly one 120 × 12 rectangle — 4 704 pixels of
it, and not one anywhere else in the row — and at the 900 pt minimum it does
not differ at all.

**The bar and not the whole window, and that is the one thing this script
promises about a future it cannot see.** A cross-build comparison holds the
current tree to a tree that ages: phase 6 adds inspector sections, phase 7
touches the export chrome, and the first of them would make a whole-window
comparison fail with the meter itself untouched — a proof that breaks on
being right, in a repository whose rule is that every earlier phase's script
re-runs unchanged. So sections 3, 5 and 6 score only what happened inside
`bar_rect`, the row the meter went into and whose slack it took, and print
what changed elsewhere without scoring it. Nothing is lost by it: all five
chrome mutations below are bar-local, because every way a level meter can be
wrong is a way the timeline bar looks wrong. **Section 3b is the check that
the scoping works** — the same reference render against a current one whose
PLAYHEAD has moved, which changes the toolbar's timecode and the ruler's
line and nothing the bar draws. It is the shape of every later phase's chrome
change, staged: the window differs in four places and the bar still differs
in exactly the meter's 4 704 pixels. (Measured, with that scoping reverted:
the same pair fails, 80/81.) What a change to the BAR itself would do is not
covered and is not meant to be — a phase that redraws this row is a phase
that has to re-baseline this comparison, and section 3's rectangle
measurements are what will tell it so.

The instrument itself is guarded the same way. The reference is compiled with
the CURRENT `harness/main.swift` under `-D HARNESS_REFERENCE_BUILD` — one
general flag, not a per-phase one, so a later phase's mode goes behind the
same `#if`. A reference build
that cannot be made at all is a scored FAILURE and not a `sys.exit`: it is
the only thing here that reaches backwards in the history, so it is the only
thing that can rot on its own, and it must not take the model checks — which
need no reference at all — down with it. A failed current harness build also
leaves the independent gain checks running; meter requests and renders cannot.

**One harness change, and the phase's plan said there would not be one.**
Wave 2B measured the meter's rect and reported the model reachable without
touching `harness/main.swift`, by compiling `app/Sources/LevelMeter.swift`
alone against a stand-in for the two types it borrows — and that was true
when they wrote it. Wave 6 then moved `LevelMeterEnvelope`'s search into
`MediaPeaks.envelope`, so the app would have ONE spelling of the plan's mix
rule rather than the two phase 5 shipped with; `MediaPeaks` needs
`ProjectSnapshot`, `ReelTime` and `MediaImporter`, and standing those in
would make this script measure its own arithmetic instead of the app's. So

(at least one) is under `/usr/lib/` or `/System/Library/`, or is an
  `@rpath/Sparkle.framework/` path;
* D40 / D41 — the Release / Distribution bundle holds
  `Contents/Resources/Licenses/<library>/<file>` for every licence text of
  every pin, byte-identical to `build/codecs/licenses/<library>/<file>`;
* D42 / D43 — the Release / Distribution bundle's
  `Contents/Resources/Acknowledgements.txt` has a header for every shipped crate
  (name and version), each pin, Sparkle at `project.yml`'s version, Slaude at
  `agent/Package.resolved`'s revision, the model and each bundled font, and none
  of another kind;
* D44 / D45 — the Release binary holds `RCDevGraphicLinkLoopbackHTTP`, the
  dev-only switch that lets a `framejob://` link fetch from `http://127.0.0.1`
  (spec §11 G-49 (l)): the POSITIVE CONTROL, without which D45 would pass for
  a renamed switch; the Distribution binary does not hold it;
* D46 / D47 — the Release / Distribution Info.plist has exactly one
  `CFBundleURLTypes` row and its `CFBundleURLSchemes` is exactly
  `["framejob"]` (G-49 (i): a Debug build's `framejob-debug` never reaches
  either).

If D1 fails, D4, D5, D12 and D13 FAIL too, and so does each when its binary
or helper is missing; D14 FAILs when the Distribution binary is, D25 and

`agent/Package.resolved` is missing or unreadable, naming which. D17–D20

readable `tools` or the dev names cannot be read. A missing `codesign`, a

content.content:
# The screen catalog

One Markdown file per Frame Job screen: how to reach it, what to capture, and a
description of it for someone who has never seen the app — the text a design
request carries beside the pictures. `tools/proof/screens.py` reads every file
here, drives its own Frame Job into each screen over MCP and the dev tools, and
writes the PNGs (light and dark) and one `screens.md` pairing each picture with
its prose into `tools/proof/work/screens/<date>/`. The prose lives here so it
changes with the screens; the pictures are made fresh each run and are not kept
in the repository.

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py            # the whole catalog; tools/proof/README.md has the rest
```

## A screen file

The file's first non-blank line is ```` ```json screen ````; the block ends at
the next line that is exactly ```` ``` ````. What is between is one JSON object,
the front block. Everything after the closing fence is the prose, copied into
`screens.md` verbatim. The file's name without `.md` is the screen's id, and the
screens run in name order.

```json
{
  "title": "Clip inspector — Sound",
  "project": "demo",
  "steps": [
    {"call": "set_selection", "args": {"clips": ["$clip:tone"]}},
    {"call": "set_playhead", "args": {"t": 1500000}}
  ],
  "captures": [
    {"name": "window", "window": "editor"},
    {"name": "inspector", "window": "editor", "view": "inspector"}
  ],
  "after": [],
  "expect": [{"capture": "inspector", "visible_text": "Gain"}]
}
```

- `title` (required): the heading in `screens.md`.
- `project` (required): `null` (no project open — Welcome, Settings), `"empty"`
  or `"demo"`, a fixture `screens.py` builds (below). It is opened before the
  steps run.
- `steps`: calls, in order, `{"call": TOOL, "args": {…}}`. `TOOL` is one of
  `STEP_TOOLS`: `set_selection`, `set_playhead`, `detect_silence`,
  `perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`,
  `transcript_view` (the Transcript tab's find bar, screen 11d). Never give
  `args` a `project`: `screens.py` adds the fixture's path to every call. A
  string `"$clip:<name>"` anywhere in `args` becomes that fixture clip's id.
  `"until_absent": KEY, "within": SECONDS` repeats the call every 0.5 s until its
  answer has no `KEY` (for example `detect_silence` until `pending_peaks` is
  gone), and fails the screen after `within`.
- `captures` (at least one): `{"name", "window", "view"?}`. `window` is
  `welcome`, `settings`, `editor`, `sheet` (the sheet attached to the editor) or
  `recorder` (the New Recording panel); `view` — `toolbar`, `preview`,
  `inspector` or `timeline` — captures one region of the editor. Each capture is
  taken light and dark: `<id>.<name>.light.png` and `.dark.png`, each with its
  layout dump beside it. The two looks come from two instances, one launched
  with `-RCDevAppearance light` and one with `-RCDevAppearance dark`, so every
  step runs once per look; a capture that answers any other appearance fails the
  screen. Both instances are launched with `-RCDevCaptureScale 2` (spec §11
  #539), so every capture is drawn at 2× whatever display its window opened on;
  a capture that answers any other `scale` fails the screen.
- `after`: steps run after the captures, to put the app back — `cancel_sheet`
  for a screen that opened a sheet. A screen that leaves a sheet attached fails.
- `expect`: `{"capture", "visible_text" | "no_visible_text"}`, checked on every
  look's layout dump: some view that is not hidden must read exactly that text,
  or none may. A failed expect fails the screen and deletes its pictures. Use it
  where a screen depends on something the pins or the fixture decide (the
  Settings window must say `No API key is set.`; the Sound sub-tab's Volume
  section must be open).
- `skip`: a reason. A screen with a non-empty `skip` runs nothing and is scored
  a skip with that reason; it needs only `title`.

Anything else — an unknown key, a missing required one, a step with its own
`project`, a `$clip:` name the fixture lacks, a menu path that is not a leaf of
the menu or not a `sheet`/`window` item or a view toggle — fails the screen as `front block: …`
before any of its steps runs.

```json screen
{
  "title": "Settings",
  "project": null,
  "steps": [{"call": "perform_menu_item", "args": {"path": ["Frame Job", "Settings…"]}}],
  "captures": [{"name": "window", "window": "settings"}],
  "expect": [{"capture": "window", "visible_text": "Copy MCP Command"},
             {"capture": "window",
              "visible_text": "An MCP client such as Claude Code uses Frame Job's tools through framejob-mcp, a helper inside this app. It reaches Frame Job over a local socket that only programs you run can open."},
             {"capture": "window", "visible_text": "Anthropic API key:"},
             {"capture": "window", "visible_text": "AssemblyAI API key:"},
             {"capture": "window", "visible_text": "No API key is set."},
             {"capture": "window", "visible_text": "Compact when context reaches"},
             {"capture": "window",
              "visible_text": "Frame Job's own estimate at LiteLLM prices, from its spend ledger. The Anthropic Console shows what your account was billed."},
             {"capture": "window", "visible_text": "Background render"},
             {"capture": "window", "no_visible_text": "API key:"}]
}
```

Settings (Frame Job ▸ Settings…) has four sections, one under the other: MCP,
Assistant, Transcription and Playback. The first is where a person finds how to connect
an MCP client such as Claude Code to Frame Job (spec §11 MC-7); the second is
where they give Frame Job an Anthropic API key, choose the model for the
Assistant tab, and set how a long conversation is kept in bounds; the third is
where they give it an AssemblyAI API key, so that the Generate Captions sheet
can transcribe in the cloud instead of on this Mac; the fourth is where they
say whether Frame Job draws a window's graphics ahead while it is left alone
(spec §11 G-38).

The "MCP" section opens with its bold heading alone, with no ⓘ. Under it, two
short paragraphs in 13 pt black (white in dark), visible rather than in a
popover: "An MCP client such as Claude Code uses Frame Job's tools through
framejob-mcp, a helper inside this app. It reaches Frame Job over a local socket
that only programs you run can open." and "If Frame Job isn't running, the first
tool call opens it in the background. To add Frame Job to Claude Code, copy the
command and run it in Terminal." Then the helper's path inside this copy of
the app, ending `Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp`, in 12 pt monospace black,
selectable, wrapping by character when it is long. Then a "Copy MCP Command"
button (a white square button with a thin outline), and under it an empty
status line: after a press it reads "Copied. Paste it into Terminal and press
Return.", and in a copy of Frame Job without the helper the button is dimmed and
the line reads "framejob-mcp is missing from this copy of Frame Job." Nothing in
the section is selected when the window opens; the Anthropic key field has the
focus.

The Assistant, Transcription and Playback sections each open with their bold heading
and, just after it, a small mid-grey ⓘ icon about the height of the heading's capitals, darkening while the pointer
is on it. Resting on an ⓘ for about a third of a second opens a standard macOS
popover under it — the rounded bubble with an arrow (spec §11 SH-5) — holding
that section's explanation in 13 pt black (white in dark), in short
paragraphs; leaving the icon closes it, and clicking the icon opens it and
keeps it open until it is clicked again or a click lands elsewhere. The
popover is not in the capture: it opens only under the pointer or a click,
and nothing in the catalog hovers or clicks.

Under the "Assistant" heading: an "Anthropic API key:" field, empty, whose
placeholder reads "Paste your key"; a "Model:" field, empty, whose grey
placeholder reads "claude-opus-5-5" (the default when it is left blank); then
the chat settings, two rows of their own. The first is a ticked checkbox

# Spec §11 — decisions: Publishing a build

Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
[`README.md`](README.md).

These were made with no road map: the pipeline is Rasterize's (`~/devel/rasterize`'s
`.github/workflows/publish.yml`), carried over on 2026-10-04, and a decision below says so
where Frame Job's differs, and why.

- **PUB-1 — A build for another person's Mac is made only by GitHub Actions, on a push to the
  `publish` branch: a Developer ID-signed, notarized, stapled `FrameJob.dmg` attached to a GitHub
  Release tagged `v<version>`.** `.github/workflows/publish.yml` is the whole pipeline. The
  certificate and the notarization key are secrets of the repository's `publish` environment,
  which only the `publish` branch may use; the team ID is one of them and is never written in
  the repository. Every local build stays ad-hoc signed (`CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY: "-"`), so `make
  app`, `make dist` and every proof need no certificate and no keychain prompt, which an agent's
  headless build could not answer. Risks accepted: the workflow does not run `make test` (its
  proofs depend on host state a runner does not have), so the tree pushed to `publish` is as
  tested as whoever pushed it left it; there is no updater, so a person re-downloads to update;
  and while the repository is private a release's DMG is downloadable only by people with access
  to it.
  **Amended by NM-3** (rename R0): `Reelcut.dmg` is now `FrameJob.dmg` (NM-2's exception: GitHub
  rewrites a space in a release asset's name to a dot); the DMG's volume name Reelcut is now
  "Frame Job", and the release's title "Reelcut <version>" is now "Frame Job <version>".
  **Amended by PUB-6**: there is an updater, Sparkle 2 in the published build, so an installed
  copy updates itself; the private-repository risk ends when the owner makes the repository
  public, which comes before the first Sparkle-enabled publish.
- **PUB-2 — The version is `<MAJOR.MINOR>.<run number>`, the build number is the run number, and
  the base is the `VERSION` file at the root, exactly as in Rasterize (the owner's choice,
  2026-10-04).** `make project` passes the file to xcodegen as `RC_BASE_VERSION`, `project.yml`
  sets `MARKETING_VERSION` from it, and `Info.plist` reads `$(MARKETING_VERSION)` and
  `$(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)`; a local build reads "0.2 (0)". The workflow reads the file,
  refuses anything that is not two integers, and overrides both settings on its command line.
  The scheme's one trap is that a BARE `xcodegen generate` writes a blank version, so `make
  project` is the only way the project is generated: it stops when `VERSION` is missing,
  `tree_copy.py` copies the file into every proof's tree copy (whose `make app` runs `make
  project` there), and `published_check.py`'s P15 fails a bundle whose version is blank, in
  `make dist` and in the workflow. Risks accepted: the third number does not reset when the
  base is bumped (0.2.41 is followed by 0.3.42), and the run counter belongs to the workflow
  FILE, so renaming or recreating `publish.yml` restarts it and build numbers go backwards.

# Spec §11 — decisions: Publishing a build

Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
[`README.md`](README.md).

These were made with no road map: the pipeline is Rasterize's (`~/devel/rasterize`'s
`.github/workflows/publish.yml`), carried over on 2026-10-04, and a decision below says so
where Frame Job's differs, and why.

- **PUB-1 — A build for another person's Mac is made only by GitHub Actions, on a push to the
  `publish` branch: a Developer ID-signed, notarized, stapled `FrameJob.dmg` attached to a GitHub
  Release tagged `v<version>`.** `.github/workflows/publish.yml` is the whole pipeline. The
  certificate and the notarization key are secrets of the repository's `publish` environment,
  which only the `publish` branch may use; the team ID is one of them and is never written in
  the repository. Every local build stays ad-hoc signed (`CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY: "-"`), so `make
  app`, `make dist` and every proof need no certificate and no keychain prompt, which an agent's
  headless build could not answer. Risks accepted: the workflow does not run `make test` (its
  proofs depend on host state a runner does not have), so the tree pushed to `publish` is as
  tested as whoever pushed it left it; there is no updater, so a person re-downloads to update;
  and while the repository is private a release's DMG is downloadable only by people with access
  to it.
  **Amended by NM-3** (rename R0): `Reelcut.dmg` is now `FrameJob.dmg` (NM-2's exception: GitHub
  rewrites a space in a release asset's name to a dot); the DMG's volume name Reelcut is now
  "Frame Job", and the release's title "Reelcut <version>" is now "Frame Job <version>".
  **Amended by PUB-6**: there is an updater, Sparkle 2 in the published build, so an installed
  copy updates itself; the private-repository risk ends when the owner makes the repository
  public, which comes before the first Sparkle-enabled publish.
- **PUB-2 — The version is `<MAJOR.MINOR>.<run number>`, the build number is the run number, and
  the base is the `VERSION` file at the root, exactly as in Rasterize (the owner's choice,
  2026-10-04).** `make project` passes the file to xcodegen as `RC_BASE_VERSION`, `project.yml`
  sets `MARKETING_VERSION` from it, and `Info.plist` reads `$(MARKETING_VERSION)` and
  `$(CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION)`; a local build reads "0.2 (0)". The workflow reads the file,
  refuses anything that is not two integers, and overrides both settings on its command line.
  The scheme's one trap is that a BARE `xcodegen generate` writes a blank version, so `make
  project` is the only way the project is generated: it stops when `VERSION` is missing,
  `tree_copy.py` copies the file into every proof's tree copy (whose `make app` runs `make
  project` there), and `published_check.py`'s P15 fails a bundle whose version is blank, in
  `make dist` and in the workflow. Risks accepted: the third number does not reset when the
  base is bumped (0.2.41 is followed by 0.3.42), and the run counter belongs to the workflow
  FILE, so renaming or recreating `publish.yml` restarts it and build numbers go backwards.

content.content:
# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, and `engines` in `package.json` sets the Node it needs. `README.md` has
the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list); SiteTitle, ThemeSelect,
                        PageTitle and Hero are the theme's Starlight overrides
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/assets/             logo.svg (the Frame Job mark, the splash hero) and
                        boppa-llewyn-blocks.svg (the company mark, the header)
src/styles/             tokens.css (the design system's --bl-* tokens, copied whole from the
                        handoff), boppa-llewyn.css (the theme, shared with Doctored's site)
                        and frame-job.css (this site's components in it); README "Theme"
src/fonts/, public/fonts/  the theme's self-hosted faces and their licence
src/site.ts             the header badge's version, read from the repository's VERSION
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`, `open_link`, `cache_ledger`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
  The Leveler's own words are the one exception in prose: leveler, leveling and leveled follow
  the app everywhere on the site, so no page spells the feature two ways (spec §11 #526 as
  extended by #541). The JSON key stays `leveller`, in a code span.
  `tools/proof/ai_docs_r2c_proof.py --only T2` holds it.
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Eyebrow:** the mono label above a page's title is the name of its sidebar group. Set
  `eyebrow:` in the frontmatter only when that name is wrong for the page.
- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.

---
title: "Settings"
description: "Every control in the Settings window: connecting an MCP client, your Anthropic and AssemblyAI keys, the Assistant's model, and background rendering."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

Settings holds what belongs to you and not to a project: how an MCP client reaches Frame Job, your Anthropic key and the Assistant's model, your AssemblyAI key and region, and whether graphics render while you're idle.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Frame Job ▸ Settings…"
  keys="⌘,"
  where="Assistant tab ▸ Open Settings…"
/>

<Shot
  name="02-settings.window"
  alt="The Assistant, Transcription and Playback sections of Settings with no keys stored. Assistant has an Anthropic API key field reading Paste your key, a Model field, Compact when context reaches 300,000 tokens ticked, Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens unticked, and Save and Remove buttons. Transcription has an AssemblyAI API key field, Region set to United States, and Save, Remove, Verify and Account Page buttons. Playback has Background render ticked, starting after 5 seconds."
/>

## Opening Settings

Choose **Frame Job ▸ Settings…** (<kbd>⌘,</kbd>). It works with or without a project open, so you can set your keys from the Welcome window before you make anything. It's a window, not a sheet, and it shows the same settings whichever project is open.

The window has four sections, one under the other: **MCP**, **Assistant**, **Transcription** and **Playback**. There are no tabs. On a short screen the window stops at the screen's height and scrolls.

There's no OK or Cancel. Every control saves as you use it, and a key saves when you press its **Save** button. While it's open it's listed in the **Window** menu, so you can bring it back from behind other windows.

Other places send you here:

- With no Anthropic key, the Assistant tab shows "Add your Anthropic API key in Settings to use the assistant." and an **Open Settings…** button that opens this window.
- With AssemblyAI chosen and no key, the note above the buttons in the Generate Captions sheet, and the **Generate** button's tooltip, read "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription." The sheet doesn't open Settings for you. If every file already has a transcript it can use, you don't need a key and there's no note.
- With no AssemblyAI key and no filler transcript to use, **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…** is greyed, its title ends "(needs your AssemblyAI key)", and its tooltip is that same sentence.

[AI features and your own keys](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/) says what each key turns on.

## The info buttons

The **Assistant**, **Transcription** and **Playback** headings each carry an ⓘ button that explains the section. The MCP section has none, because its text is shown in full.

- Rest the pointer on it for about a third of a second to see the explanation. Moving away closes it.
- Click it to keep the explanation open. Click it again, click anywhere else, press <kbd>⎋</kbd> or close the window to end it.

VoiceOver reads it as "About Assistant", and so on for each section. With keyboard navigation on, <kbd>Space</kbd> presses it.

## MCP

This section shows how an MCP client, such as Claude Code, reaches Frame Job. Clients use `framejob-mcp`, a helper inside the app, which connects over a local socket that only programs you run can open. If Frame Job isn't running, the first tool call opens it in the background.

Under that text is the full path of the helper inside the copy you're running. You can select and copy it.

**Copy MCP Command** puts the line that registers the helper with Claude Code on the clipboard, with the path filled in and quoted for the shell:

```sh
claude mcp add --scope user framejob -- '/Applications/Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp'
```

The section then says "Copied. Paste it into Terminal and press Return."

The path is always the one for the app you opened Settings from, so copy the command again if you move Frame Job. If the helper is missing from this copy, the button is dimmed and the section says "framejob-mcp is missing from this copy of Frame Job."

The command is for Claude Code. Other clients use the same helper path in their own configuration. See [Connect a client](/mcp/connect-a-client/).

## Assistant

This section holds what the Assistant tab needs: your Anthropic key, the model, and two settings for long conversations. See [Set up the Assistant](/assistant/set-up/).

| Control | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Anthropic API key:** | A secure field. Paste a key and press **Save** or <kbd>↩</kbd>. See [How the key fields behave](#how-the-key-fields-behave). | None |
| **Model:** | The Anthropic model the Assistant uses, typed as text. Saved when you press <kbd>↩</kbd> or leave the field. Leave it blank for the default. | `claude-opus-5-5` |
| **Compact when context reaches … tokens** | When a turn ends with the conversation at or past this size, the conversation is replaced by a summary. Untick it to never compact. The number can be 20,000 to 900,000, and the field works only while the box is ticked. | On, 300,000 |
| **Clear old tool results past 150,000 tokens** | Lets Anthropic drop old tool results from what the model sees, even partway through a turn. It never drops tool search results. | Off |
| **Save** | Stores the key typed in the field, then empties the field. With the field empty it only beeps. | |
| **Remove** | Deletes the stored key. Dimmed when no key is stored. | |

There's no **Verify** button here. Your key is first used when you send a message from the Assistant tab.

**A change to the key or the model starts over.** Saving or removing the key, or changing the model, ends the conversation in every open window's Assistant tab, and the next message starts a new one. Pressing <kbd>↩</kbd> in **Model:** without changing the model that's used ends nothing.

**A change to the other two keeps going.** The compaction and clearing settings apply to every open conversation at once and end none of them. They have no **Save** button. A compaction number outside 20,000 to 900,000 beeps, and the field goes back to the stored number.

Compaction loses the frames the Assistant rendered earlier, so it renders again when it needs to look. Each clearing also adds to your bill. See [Long conversations](/assistant/context-and-compaction/).

Under the buttons is what the Assistant has cost this month, with a note that the figure is Frame Job's own estimate. See [What it costs](/assistant/cost/).

The ⓘ sums up what's sent to Anthropic, that it's billed to your key, that the Assistant asks before saving a project or writing a file to a path it chose, that graphics, fonts and pictures it adds go into the project [without asking](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/#file-writes-that-do-not-ask), where the key is kept, the blank **Model:** default and the two chat settings.

## Transcription

This section holds your AssemblyAI key and region. **File ▸ Generate Captions…** uses them with AssemblyAI chosen, and so does **Clip ▸ Remove Filler Words…**. Captions made on your Mac need no key. See [Your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/).

| Control | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **AssemblyAI API key:** | A secure field. Paste a key and press **Save** or <kbd>↩</kbd>. See [How the key fields behave](#how-the-key-fields-behave). | None |
| **Region:** | **United States** or **European Union**. Saved as soon as you pick it. | United States |
| **Save** | Stores the key typed in the field, then empties the field. With the field empty it only beeps. | |
| **Remove** | Deletes the stored key. Dimmed when no key is stored. | |
| **Verify** | Makes AssemblyAI's cheapest signed-in request, with the key and region, to check they work. | |
| **Account Page** | Opens AssemblyAI's dashboard in your browser, where you get a key and see what you've spent. | |

A transcript made in one region can't be seen from the other, so pick the region your AssemblyAI account uses. A stored region Frame Job doesn't recognise counts as United States.

**Verify** checks a key you've typed and not saved, otherwise the stored key, otherwise a key from the environment. It's dimmed with no key at all, and while a check of the same key and region is running. The line under the controls gives the answer:

| The line says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "Checking…" | The check is running. |
| "Key accepted" | AssemblyAI took the key in this region. |
| "Settings changed since this check began. Verify again." | You changed the key or the region during the check, so its answer no longer applies. |
| Any other sentence, such as "AssemblyAI refused the API key — check it in Frame Job ▸ Settings" or "No network connection" | The check failed, and the sentence says why. |

Saving or removing the key, or changing the region, reaches an open Generate Captions sheet straight away, so you don't need to reopen it.

The ⓘ explains what's uploaded, when it's deleted and what AssemblyAI charges. See [What goes to AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-privacy/).

## Playback

This section controls whether Frame Job draws graphics ahead of time while you're idle, so they play smoothly from the start.

| Control | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Background render** | While you leave Frame Job alone, it draws the graphics after the playhead in the window you used last. | On |
| **Start after … seconds** | How long you must be idle first, as a whole number from 1 to 60. Type it or use the stepper. Dimmed while **Background render** is off. | 5 |

The box and the stepper save the moment you use them, and a typed number saves when you press <kbd>↩</kbd> or leave the field. A number outside 1 to 60 beeps, and the field goes back to the stored number.

Anything you do in Frame Job stops the drawing at once and starts the wait again from zero: a key, a click, a scroll, an edit, play or a seek. An agent's calls count when they edit a project or move a playhead, and a call that only reads doesn't. Moving the pointer alone doesn't count, and neither does what you do in other apps.

Background render never runs while a window is playing, and it keeps the processor busy while it runs. Its frames are held in memory, at most a quarter of your Mac's and less when memory is short, until the window closes or newer frames replace them. It draws pictures only and changes nothing about the sound. See [Graphics playback and memory](/graphics/playback-and-memory/).

## How the key fields behave

The Anthropic and AssemblyAI fields work the same way. A saved key is never shown again.

- With a key stored, the field shows a row of dots as its placeholder. The row is always the same length, so it says nothing about your key, and the key itself is never put in the field.
- With no key stored, the field reads "Paste your key".

The line under the controls reports what happened:

| The line says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "Key saved." or "Key removed." | The press worked. |
| "No API key is set." | There's no key in the field, in storage or in the environment. It's in ordinary grey, because this isn't an error. |
| "The API key could not be saved: …" | The key file couldn't be written, and the end of the line gives the reason. The field is still emptied. A **Remove** that fails shows the same sentence with its own reason, and the stored key stays. |

[Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/) says where the keys are stored, and how a key can come from the environment.

## Agents and Settings

No agent tool reads or writes anything in Settings. Your keys, the model, the region and **Background render** are set only by you, in this window.

An agent's cloud tools, `transcribe` with the AssemblyAI engine and `transcribe_for_fillers`, do use the key and region saved here, so you have to set the key first. Without one they stop at the point they would send, with "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription." A file that already has a transcript they can use needs no key. See [How an agent reaches Frame Job](/mcp/overview/).

## Related

- [AI features and your own keys](/getting-started/ai-and-your-keys/)
- [Connect a client](/mcp/connect-a-client/)
- [Set up the Assistant](/assistant/set-up/)
- [Your AssemblyAI key](/captions/assemblyai-key/)
- [Graphics playback and memory](/graphics/playback-and-memory/)
- [What Frame Job remembers](/reference/remembered-choices/)
- [Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/)

title: Open source and notices
description: Frame Job's Apache License 2.0, and where to read the third-party notices every copy of the app carries.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Frame Job is open source. This page gives its licence, and says where to find the notices for the third-party software it includes.

<AtAGlance
  where="Frame Job.app ▸ Contents/Resources/Acknowledgements.txt"
/>

## Frame Job's licence

Frame Job is released under the Apache License, Version 2.0. The full text is the [LICENSE file](https://github.com/kpgalligan/framejob/blob/main/LICENSE) at the root of the repository.

## Third-party notices

Every copy of the app carries `Acknowledgements.txt`, which lists every third-party notice the app owes, each with its licence text. It's written at each build, from the Rust crates, the Assistant helper's Swift package (Slaude), Sparkle, the encoders, the voice-activity model and the fonts.

There's no entry for it in the About panel. To read it:

<Steps>

1. In the Finder, right-click Frame Job and choose **Show Package Contents**.

2. Open `Contents/Resources/Acknowledgements.txt`.

</Steps>

## What carries its own licence

Some of what ships with Frame Job keeps its own licence, beside it in the app or listed in `Acknowledgements.txt`.

| Part | Licence | Where its text is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fonts: Anton, Bebas Neue, Darker Grotesque, IBM Plex Mono, Montserrat, Source Sans 3 and Source Serif 4 | SIL Open Font License | `Contents/Resources/Fonts/`, one `OFL-` file for each family |
| The voice-activity model, Silero VAD | MIT | `Contents/Resources/Models/LICENSE` |
| SVT-AV1 and libvpx, the [AV1 and VP9](/export/av1-and-vp9/) encoders | BSD 3-Clause Clear and BSD 3-Clause | `Contents/Resources/Licenses/svt-av1/` and `Contents/Resources/Licenses/libvpx/`, with their patent texts |
| A patched copy of tiny-skia, which draws [graphics](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/) | BSD 3-Clause | `Acknowledgements.txt` |

The published app also includes Sparkle, for [updates](/getting-started/updates/). A copy you build yourself has no updater.

## Related

- [Requirements and install](/getting-started/requirements-and-install/)
- [Updates](/getting-started/updates/)

## Playback

This section controls whether Frame Job draws graphics ahead of time while you're idle, so they play smoothly from the start.

| Control | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Background render** | While you leave Frame Job alone, it draws the graphics after the playhead in the window you used last. | On |
| **Start after … seconds** | How long you must be idle first, as a whole number from 1 to 60. Type it or use the stepper. Dimmed while **Background render** is off. | 5 |

The box and the stepper save the moment you use them, and a typed number saves when you press <kbd>↩</kbd> or leave the field. A number outside 1 to 60 beeps, and the field goes back to the stored number.

Anything you do in Frame Job stops the drawing at once and starts the wait again from zero: a key, a click, a scroll, an edit, play or a seek. An agent's calls count when they edit a project or move a playhead, and a call that only reads doesn't. Moving the pointer alone doesn't count, and neither does what you do in other apps.

Background render never runs while a window is playing, and it keeps the processor busy while it runs. Its frames are held in memory, at most a quarter of your Mac's and less when memory is short, until the window closes or newer frames replace them. It draws pictures only and changes nothing about the sound. See [Graphics playback and memory](/graphics/playback-and-memory/).

## How the key fields behave

The Anthropic and AssemblyAI fields work the same way. A saved key is never shown again.

- With a key stored, the field shows a row of dots as its placeholder. The row is always the same length, so it says nothing about your key, and the key itself is never put in the field.
- With no key stored, the field reads "Paste your key".

The line under the controls reports what happened:

| The line says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "Key saved." or "Key removed." | The press worked. |
| "No API key is set." | There's no key in the field, in storage or in the environment. It's in ordinary grey, because this isn't an error. |
| "The API key could not be saved: …" | The key file couldn't be written, and the end of the line gives the reason. The field is still emptied. A **Remove** that fails shows the same sentence with its own reason, and the stored key stays. |

[Where Frame Job keeps its files](/reference/file-locations/) says where the keys are stored, and how a key can come from the environment.

## Agents and Settings

No agent tool reads or writes anything in Settings. Your keys, the model, the region and **Background render** are set only by you, in this window.

An agent's cloud tools, `transcribe` with the AssemblyAI engine and `transcribe_for_fillers`, do use the key and region saved here, so you have to set the key first. Without one they stop at the point they would send, with "No AssemblyAI API key is set. Set one in Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Transcription." A file that already has a transcript they can use needs no key. See [How an agent reaches Frame Job](/mcp/overview/).

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Frame Job is open source. This page gives its licence, and says where to find the notices for the third-party software it includes.

<AtAGlance
  where="Frame Job.app ▸ Contents/Resources/Acknowledgements.txt"
/>

## Frame Job's licence

Frame Job is released under the Apache License, Version 2.0. The full text is the [LICENSE file](https://github.com/kpgalligan/framejob/blob/main/LICENSE) at the root of the repository.

## Third-party notices

Every copy of the app carries `Acknowledgements.txt`, which lists every third-party notice the app owes, each with its licence text. It's written at each build, from the Rust crates, the Assistant helper's Swift package (Slaude), Sparkle, the encoders, the voice-activity model and the fonts.

There's no entry for it in the About panel. To read it:

<Steps>

1. In the Finder, right-click Frame Job and choose **Show Package Contents**.

2. Open `Contents/Resources/Acknowledgements.txt`.

</Steps>

## What carries its own licence

Some of what ships with Frame Job keeps its own licence, beside it in the app or listed in `Acknowledgements.txt`.

| Part | Licence | Where its text is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fonts: Anton, Bebas Neue, Darker Grotesque, IBM Plex Mono, Montserrat, Source Sans 3 and Source Serif 4 | SIL Open Font License | `Contents/Resources/Fonts/`, one `OFL-` file for each family |
| The voice-activity model, Silero VAD | MIT | `Contents/Resources/Models/LICENSE` |
| SVT-AV1 and libvpx, the [AV1 and VP9](/export/av1-and-vp9/) encoders | BSD 3-Clause Clear and BSD 3-Clause | `Contents/Resources/Licenses/svt-av1/` and `Contents/Resources/Licenses/libvpx/`, with their patent texts |
| A patched copy of tiny-skia, which draws [graphics](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/) | BSD 3-Clause | `Acknowledgements.txt` |

The published app also includes Sparkle, for [updates](/getting-started/updates/). A copy you build yourself has no updater.

## Related

- [Requirements and install](/getting-started/requirements-and-install/)
- [Updates](/getting-started/updates/)

- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

`screens.py` captures at 2× on any display (`-RCDevCaptureScale 2`). To refresh a few screens,
run it with `--only` and import those files without `--used`, which first empties
`src/assets/screens/`.

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here, and a new feature adds its row to
`src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, a
page that names something internal, or `docs/guide/` (the retired user guide) existing or a link
into it; its `--guide` row also runs in `make gate`'s `names` step.
# Manual checks

The standing list of checks only a person at the machine can do: things
that need eyes, ears, a real mouse and keyboard, a second display, a real
network, a real API key or macOS permissions. Everything a script can
measure is already in `tools/proof/` and is not repeated here.

**When to run it.** Run every section before a release. Between releases,
run the sections whose area changed. Unless a check says otherwise, run it
in both appearances (System Settings ▸ Appearance, Light then Dark).

## Setup, once per run

1. Build: `make app`.
2. Open the Release app from the Finder, or with
   `open "build/Build/Products/Release/Frame Job.app"`. **Not from a terminal**:
   a terminal-launched app's permissions (Screen Recording, Microphone)
   belong to the terminal, not to Frame Job. Only REC-3, REC-7, REC-8's
   step 6 and HS-2 launch from a terminal on purpose.
3. Have to hand:
   - **Real footage**: a 1080p movie with sound, a long recording (twenty
     minutes or more), an AAC file and a WAV file.
   - **Synthetic test media**, where a check names it: make it once with the
     `ffmpeg` lines under "Make the test media once" in
     `tools/proof/README.md` (into `tools/proof/media/`).
   - **Graphics projects** (GR): `RC_PROOF_APP=release python3 tools/proof/graphics_playback_samples.py`
     builds `Playback-1080p`, `Playback-4K`, `Error-card` and
     `Playback-4K-animated` into `tools/proof/work/playback-check/`. Rebuild them on a fresh checkout.
   - **Keys**: your own AssemblyAI key for Cloud captions (Frame Job ▸
     Settings… ▸ Transcription) and your own Anthropic API key for the
     Assistant (Frame Job ▸ Settings… ▸ Assistant). No script ever uses a real
     key.
4. **The compositor's timing log** (PB-2, PB-3):
   `defaults write com.kgalligan.FrameJob FrameJobCompositorTiming -bool YES`,
   relaunch, and read it in Console.app filtered on `[framejob] compositor`
   (average and worst milliseconds per 120 frames). Turn it off afterwards
   with `defaults delete com.kgalligan.FrameJob FrameJobCompositorTiming`.

## Reporting a failure

content.content:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""#554 — every proof's mutant anchors, counted in the tree. `tools/proof/README.md`'s
"Mutant anchors (mutant_anchors.py)" is the long form.

    python3 tools/proof/mutant_anchors.py              # the check (make test)
    python3 tools/proof/mutant_anchors.py --list       # every table and what was read from it
    python3 tools/proof/mutant_anchors.py --selftest   # the reader over synthetic proofs (make test)
    python3 tools/proof/mutant_anchors.py --mutant count-any|skip-unreadable|pins-one-way|\\
        missing-file-zero|no-entry-check|loose-file-passes|copies-counted|pin-per-anchor

A proof's mutant is an anchor (a piece of source text) and its replacement; its applier demands
that the anchor occurs exactly once in a file of the tree. When the source moves, the anchor rots,
and nothing said so until someone ran the mutant. This reads every `tools/proof/**/*.py` (not
`work/`), finds each mutant table, and counts each anchor in the file it names: exactly once, or
the run fails naming the proof, the table, the mutant, the count and the file.

A proof is READ, never imported: its file is parsed, and a table's expression is evaluated in a
namespace that runs only the top-level statements that bind or add to a name the table needs (a
constant, a helper `def`, a later `T[k] = …` or `T.update(…)`), each at most once, on demand. An
import of a sibling proof is a proxy read the same way; a statement that merely sits at top level
(`proof_app.binary()`, `sys.exit`) never runs. So a table's expression must be pure.

What is a table: a top-level name ending `MUTANTS`, `MUTANT_EDITS`, the pair `MUTANT_FILE` with
`MUTANT_ANCHOR` or `MUTANT_EDITS`, and `MUTANT` bound to a tuple. A name bound by an import is the
other proof's table, and is checked there. An entry's edits are read by three rules: a file
followed by an anchor and a replacement (R1); a file followed by a list of (anchor, replacement)
pairs (R2); and, for a table whose file is implicit in its applier, a row in HINTS (R3). A dict
entry with its own `file` and `anchor` keys is read by those. An edit that is in two tables
(`CLOUD_MUTANTS[name] = …MUTANTS[name]`, `MUTANTS.update(DEEP_MUTANTS)`) is counted once, under
the first table in path and source order: a copy is the same mutant name with the same anchor in
the same file.

Nothing is passed over silently. Each of these fails by name:
- a table that cannot be evaluated (UNREADABLE, with the exception);
- a table no anchor was read from, unless SWITCHES holds it with its exact mutant count;
- a mutant no anchor was read from in a table that has some, unless UNANCHORED names it;
- a source file named in an entry that no rule took as an edit's file (a half-read entry);
- an edit's file that is nowhere, or a bare name found under two folders;
- an anchor that occurs 0 or 2+ times, unless ROTTED holds its mutant with where it is filed
  (a table in EVERY has an applier that replaces every occurrence, so its anchors need one or
  more). ROTTED is decided per MUTANT: a pinned mutant's anchors that still count are counted,
  and only its dead ones are held, so a mutant with one dead edit of two can be pinned;
- another top-level name containing `MUTANT`, unless NOT_TABLES names it (`MUTANT = None`,
  an instrument's own switch, needs no row);
- a proof with the literal `--mutant` and no table, unless NO_TABLE names it;
- a pin that no longer applies, in either direction (a row for a table that now has anchors, a
  count that is off, a ROTTED mutant with no dead anchor counted under that table, a name that
  is gone).

A `--mutant` runs the selftest alone under one of the reader's own switches and must fail exactly
its rows (EXPECTED).
"""

import argparse
import ast
import builtins
import collections
import re
import shutil
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
PROOF = "tools/proof"
SELF = "mutant_anchors.py"
SCRATCH = ROOT / PROOF / "work/mutant-anchors-selftest"
TABLE = re.compile(r"^(?:[A-Z0-9]+_)*MUTANTS$|^MUTANT_EDITS$")
SOURCE = re.compile(r"^[\w+./-]+\.(?:swift|rs|metal|ts|js|mjs|h|m|c|py|toml|yml|json|sh|plist"
                    r"|entitlements)$|^(?:[\w+.-]+/)*Makefile$")
# Where a bare file name may live. A name found under two of them is ambiguous, never guessed.
BASES = ("", "app/Sources", "app/Resources/Shaders", "app/Bridging", "app", "core/src",
         "core/include", "core", "graphic/src", "graphic", "mcp-proxy/src", "mcp-proxy",
         "agent", "tools/proof")
MUTATORS = {"update", "append", "extend", "add", "insert", "setdefault", "pop", "remove",
            "discard", "clear"}
EXPECTED = {
    "count-any": {"A3"},
    "skip-unreadable": {"U1", "U3"},
    "pins-one-way": {"P2", "P3", "P4", "P6", "P8", "P10", "P11"},
    "missing-file-zero": {"F1"},
    "no-entry-check": {"E1", "E3"},
    "loose-file-passes": {"E2"},
    "copies-counted": {"C2", "P11"},
    "pin-per-anchor": {"P9", "P10", "P11"},
}
MUTANT = None

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The pins. Every row is exact: a row that no longer applies fails the run.

# R3: a table whose file is implicit in its applier. proof → table → (file, shape), where shape
# says what an entry is: "pair" (anchor, replacement, …), "anchor" (anchor, …), or "pairs"
# ([(anchor, replacement) or (anchor, replacement, file), …], …). Each row was read off the
# applier named beside it.

modal run loop, or neither — and the checks that hold `inventory.json` to
the tree (road map 11, V1).

`inventory.json` is READ BY HAND, site first: every line the grep below
finds is traced to the menu selectors that reach it, synchronously
(`reached_from`: the action method reaches the site before it returns) or
later (`reached_after`: from a sheet or panel completion, an async hop or an
AppKit delegate callback, with the `via` line and the `gate` that must hold).
Every other live selector is read to `none`, `window` or `framework`.
The grep counts the APP-MODAL `presentError(` (road map 11's V2b) — the
`presentError(_:)` / `NSApp.presentError(_:)` that runs a modal loop — and
not the sheet form `presentError(_:modalFor:…)`, which is not modal.

  I1  every leaf of `buildMainMenu()` (the probe's `menu` mode) has its
      selector in `selectors`, and every row there names a live selector;
  I2  the grep's sites and `sites` are one-to-one, each line holding its token
      and lying in its entry's `func`; a site is FOUND BY ITS TOKEN AND ITS
      ENCLOSING FUNCTION, not its line (#166, #168): `resolve` pairs the
      inventory's sites with the grep's per (file, token, func) — `func` the
      nearest `func NAME` or `init(` declaration at or above the line — in
      line order, whenever the two counts agree, so a line added above a
      site moves its pin instead of failing it; where they disagree each pin
      stands as written. A site removed and another added in one file and
      token no longer balance unless both are in one function, so a swap
      across functions is reported (K4);
  I3  every citation is checked for content (#168). A citation is a SITE ref,
      `app/Sources/<F>.swift:<N>` naming a key of `sites` (read at its
      resolved line), or an ANCHORED ref, ``app/Sources/<F>.swift `<anchor>` ``,
      whose anchor is a piece of the line meant and occurs exactly once in
      `<F>`. Each `code` item is exactly one citation; `note`, `via`, `gate`
      and `other_caller` hold citations in prose; any other `<F>.swift:<N>`
      is a problem, as is a line citation that is not a site, an anchor
      missing or not unique, and a `reached_after` whose `via` cites nothing.
      A `modal` selector cites a line holding a loop token, a `sheet` one a
      sheet token; every `reached_from` / `reached_after` selector names a
      row; a selector in the `reached_from` of a `runModal` or loop-token
      site is `modal` (`reached_after` never forces a verdict);
  I4  the checker over a copy missing one selector and one site reports
      exactly those two (the first selector no site references, and the
      first site no citation names by its line).

`python3 tools/proof/capture_spike/inventory.py --check` is a line of
`make test`: no app, no probe, no build, in a fresh `work/inventory_check/`.

  K1  I2 and I3 over the tree have no problem (I1 needs the probe, so it is
      `v2_menu.py`'s H1); its detail lists the pins found at another line;
  K2  CONTROL: a copy of `app/Sources` with three blank lines put at the top
      of every file that holds a site or is cited by an anchor has no I2 or
      I3 problem;
  K3  CONTROL: a fresh copy, the inventory's site keys first rewritten
      through `resolve`, then the line of the first rewritten site blanked:
      the checker reports exactly that site under I2;
  K4  CONTROL: a fresh copy, the keys rewritten, the first site's line
      blanked and `func b13Swap() { <that line> }` appended as the file's
      last line — a swap in one file and token: I2 reports exactly that site
      (its line does not hold its token) and the appended line (a grep site
      missing from the inventory);
  K5  CONTROL: the first anchored `code` citation (selectors sorted) with an
      invisible U+2063 appended to its anchor: `check` reports exactly that
      selector under I3 beyond the tree's own problems.

Every control that writes into its copy calls `_forget(root)` after its last
write and before its `check`, because `line_of` caches each file it reads.

content.content:
# 4.1 Toolbar

44 pt, `BarView(border: .bottom)`, 12 pt padding, 12 pt between clusters, with
a 1 pt `DS.border` rule between them.

- **Transport**: six `GhostButton`s at 34 × 26 pt on the square button radius,
  19 pt symbols, 2 pt gaps — go to start, previous edit point, play/pause,
  next edit point, go to end, loop (loops the in/out range when set, else all).
- **Timecode** in the mono face: a 24 pt bordered field on the button radius
  holding the current time, then the duration in `DS.mono(11)`
  (`00:00:20:12 / 00:01:00:00`), in the document's frame rate. Click to type a
  time; accepts `1:23`, `83.5`, `1:23:04`. A Document setting switches frames
  to milliseconds. Formatting and parsing are core functions
  (`rc_timecode_format` / `rc_timecode_parse`).
- **Canvas zoom** popup (Fit, 50, 100, 200 %) and a title-safe /
  action-safe guide toggle (90 % and 80 % rectangles).
- **Export…** (⌘E) is an `AccentButton`: 26 pt, square, `DS.accent`
  fill, `DS.onAccent` at 12 pt semibold, a 15 pt `square.and.arrow.up` at a
  6 pt gap. Hover lightens the fill; that is the whole state model. It is
  deliberately **not** `StickerButton`, the sheets', Settings' and the
  welcome window's 28 pt square button with no symbol (§11 SH-4).

Add Text, Add Shape, Add Marker and Duplicate are in the **timeline bar**
(§4.4), because each acts on a clip. Snapping is there too, because it is a
timeline concern.
| ⌘, | Settings… — Frame Job ▸ Settings…, the app's one window for something PERSISTED beyond view state (road map 6 §5d): four panes, "MCP" (§11 MC-7), holding a visible blurb on how an MCP client reaches Frame Job, the bundled helper's path and the Copy MCP Command button, then "Assistant" (road map 12 A2), holding the Anthropic key and the model (§11 AI-8, AI-11) with no Verify, the chat settings (§11 AI-20) and the month's spend line and its note (§11 P-7), under it "Transcription", holding the AssemblyAI key, the region and a Verify button, and last "Playback", holding Background render and its delay (§11 G-38); the Assistant, Transcription and Playback headings each carry an info button whose popover holds the pane's explanation (§11 SH-5). macOS's own place for the item and its own key; the nudge pair below is the BARE `,` and `.`, so nothing is displaced. A nil-target selector on `AppDelegate`, so it resolves with no document open, as New Project does |
24:| [`04.1-toolbar.md`](04.1-toolbar.md) | 25 | The toolbar. |
74:| [`09-keys-and-menus.md`](09-keys-and-menus.md) | 335 | The keyboard map and every menu, and keys proposed but not yet bound. |

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The documentation site (`docs/site/`) against the tree. No app, no build, no network, stdlib
only; `pnpm build` in `docs/site/` is what proves the site renders and its links land.

A user-visible change has to reach the site, and nothing about the site's build notices a menu
item or an agent tool it has never heard of. These rows do:

  D1  every page has a title and a description;
  D2  the sidebar and the pages are one-to-one;
